title: Chuck Bryant On The Why I’m Voting Podcast
summary: Guest appearance on the I Heart Radio podcast "Why I'm Voting," hosted by Holly Frying, featuring Chuck Bryant (host of Stuff You Should Know) discussing his personal relationship with voting. Chuck recounts learning about voting late, not registering at eighteen (he recalls a mistaken belief that registering also meant draft registration), being politically awakened in college during the first Gulf War, casting his first vote in the 1996 election as a Democrat, researching down-ballot and local measures, making voting a date with his husband, enjoying voting lines in Atlanta, and voting for his five-year-old daughter's future. The episode closes with a voter registration reminder pointing to nonpartisan sites. Note: this is a promotional guest interview from a different show, not a Stuff You Should Know episode.

segments.title: Opening ad reads
segments.summary: Sponsor reads for eBay Motors, CareerBuilder, and Royal Caribbean, followed by the show introduction.

segments.title: Introduction to Why I'm Voting
segments.summary: Holly Frying introduces the series, in which podcasters discuss why they vote, and introduces guest Chuck Bryant.

segments.title: Growing up without political talk and late start in registering
segments.summary: Chuck says politics was not discussed in his household. He learned about voting in civics class but did not register at eighteen, partly due to a mistaken belief that registering also meant draft registration.

segments.title: College political awakening during the Gulf War
segments.summary: Chuck recalls that during his sophomore or junior year of college, watching the first Gulf War on CNN and living with politically active roommates led him to see the importance of being informed and involved.

segments.title: First vote and party affiliation
segments.summary: Chuck cast his first vote in the 1996 presidential election, which he describes as Bill Clinton's second run, with Ralph Nader and Ross Perot also running, and has been a Democrat since.

segments.title: Researching candidates and local ballot measures
segments.summary: Chuck explains he researches down-ballot races and local measures, using online links and asking knowledgeable people, and reads up on measures such as Sunday drinking rules in Georgia.

segments.title: Voting rituals, early voting, and voting lines
segments.summary: Chuck discusses making voting a date with his husband, preferring early voting but enjoying the community feeling of standing in lines in his mixed-race Atlanta neighborhood, including for President Obama.

segments.title: Voter registration reminder and closing
segments.summary: Chuck's message to young and older non-voters is the vote is a duty and a way to be heard; he is voting for his five-year-old daughter's future. The episode closes with a reminder to check nonpartisan registration sites such as HeadCount.org or FairVote.org.
